messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: reserved-pool node gpu-07 (az: us-east-1c) reporting repeated ECC parity spikes and thermal throttle. Marking node as DRAINING. Affected tenant: Aurora Enterprise (vpc: aurora-prod-1). Auto-evict policy triggered. Incident ID: INC-2026-357890

pagerduty: Paging Sam (on-call SRE) and Priya (runtime lead). Severity: P1. Runbook: reserved-pool-drain -> tenant-isolate -> failover to burst-reserved.

Sam: Ack. I'm on it. Pulling recent logs and kv-cache state.

Miguel: Saw the alert, joining. Is this a single node thermal or PCIe/ECC escalation?

Rohit: Initial hardware telemetry: ECC count rising on GPU channel 2, BMC reported a PSU sag and subsequent fan ramp. NIC fine. Could be beginning of hardware degradation + spot eviction-like behavior.

Priya: Noted. We need to avoid cold KV-cache misses for Aurora. If we evict without cache handoff, tail latency will spike. Any pre-warmed nodes available in the reserve pool?

Evan: I'm the customer ops liaison for Aurora. Heads-up: Aurora uses pinned VPC routing, private endpoint. They require customer-visible failover approved before IP migration. Ready to call account exec if needed.

Sam: Action plan: 1) Isolate tenant traffic from gpu-07 via routing tag  -> route aurora-prod-1 off node. 2) Trigger KV cache warm migration to pre-warmed node (if available). 3) Start replacement worker boot/attach new GPU. 4) If no warm node, spin up burst-capacity in same AZ and perform transparent swap. 5) Notify customer and request quick approval for private IP failover if needed.

Miguel: Running step 1 now: updating node-affinity rules. Command: ```sh
rbctl node drain --node gpu-07 --pool reserved-aurora
rbctl route update --tenant aurora-prod-1 --exclude-node gpu-07
```

Sam: Step 1 complete. Traffic showing 98% removal from node within 30s. LB sessions draining.

Priya: Checking KV cache state: current hotset size ~6.4GB, cache miss rate ~0.7%. We have one pre-warmed standby node in az-us-east-1c (reserved-standby-03). Preparing to migrate.

Rohit: While you migrate, I'm opening an RMA ticket and marking the physical host for replacement after we confirm tenant is stable. BMC logs saved (attached to ticket).

Evan: Customer prefers no IP changes. They allow traffic reroute to standby node but not public endpoint change. Will escalate to legal if we need IP move. Keep them in loop.

Priya: Ok we'll avoid IP move. We'll attach standby node into same VPC with traffic gateway. Initiating cache warm sync: ```sh
kv-migrate --from gpu-07 --to reserved-standby-03 --mode incremental --throttle 25MB/s
```

Miguel: kv-migrate started. ETA ~45s for 6.4GB at throttle. Monitoring miss-rate.

Sam: Meanwhile I'm triaging orchestration logs. Found one recent BMC reset 2m before ECC spike. Could be PSU transient. Marking node as non-evictable for other tenants until replacement.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic fallback policy enabled: fallback-model-variant = gpu-x32-q8 -> potential perf delta. No user traffic yet switched to fallback.

Priya: Cache migrate at 60% after 30s, miss-rate dropping. If migration completes, we can point aurora to the standby without IP change.

Evan: Sending a short status to Aurora'Ops: "We detected hardware degradation on a reserved GPU node. We're migrating your cache to a standby node in the same VPC to avoid IP changes. No customer-visible downtime expected. Will confirm when complete."

Sam: Good. Prepare failover steps once kv-migrate finishes: attach ENI, rebind routing tag to standby, verify session continuity.

Rohit: RMA created: ticket #RMA-98211. Field tech scheduled in 6 hours for PSU replacement. Marking node for physical replacement.

Miguel: kv-migrate finished. Perfs look good. Now switching route: ```sh
rbctl route rebind --tenant aurora-prod-1 --from-node gpu-07 --to-node reserved-standby-03
```

Sam: Rebind executed. Monitoring application telemetry. Latency percentiles stable (p50 unchanged, p99 up by ~3%). No request errors spike. :white_check_mark:

Priya: Runtime traces show KV hits at standby node, no stale data. Cache warm handshake successful.

Evan: Aurora confirms they see normal traffic and no failed requests. Thanks.

incident-bot: AUDIT: tenant-isolation and route-rebind events logged. Action items created: INC-2026-357890-ACTION (replace hardware, confirm post-replace soak).

Sam: Now that tenant is safe, marking gpu-07 in maintenance and setting pool capacity adjust: spin up replacement reserved node to restore pool count. ```sh
rbctl node replace --old gpu-07 --request-type reserved --az us-east-1c
```

Miguel: Replacement request queued. It may take ~12m to provision and attach. We'll keep standby as active until validated.

Priya: Adding extra monitoring: ramp up tracing retention to 10m for aurora routes and set alert if p99 > baseline + 20% for 30s.

Evan: I'm posting to Aurora account Slack channel with summary and timestamped notes. They're appreciative of the proactive handoff.

Rohit: Hardware note: after PSU swap we'll run stress test and ECC scrub. If ECC persists, escalate for full GPU/OEM replacement.

Sam: Ok wrap-up: 1) Tenant traffic migrated to reserved-standby-03 2) KV cache warm migration done 3) Replacement node requested 4) Customer notified and approved 5) Monitoring window 30m. If any regression, escalate to on-call hardware and Priya.

Tanya: Adding to post-incident: investigate BMC/PSU correlation, add health check to preemptively surface PSU sag before ECC spike. Also consider auto-warm capability for enterprise tenants with big KV sets.

Priya: Agree, will create RFC for auto-warm and preferred standby reservations for VPC customers.

Sam: Closing this coordination thread. Will update incident ticket with timeline and attach logs. Monitoring continues. If anything changes, re-open. :hand:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-357890 transitioned to MONITORING. Next check-in at +30m.
